stances_toward.note: Israel rejects the Court's jurisdiction: the warrants for Netanyahu and Gallant (21 Nov 2024) stand, the Appeals Chamber in April 2025 sent Israel's jurisdictional challenge back to the Pre-Trial Chamber without suspending them and in October 2025 rejected Israel's bid to cancel them; Germany, Poland and Hungary (until its change of government) have signalled that the warrant would not stop a visit. Rival, not adversary: Israel contests the body and does not seek its end. Bond - grievance.

relations_to.summary: The Emirate rejects the ICC outright; after the Pre-Trial Chamber issued warrants for the Emir Hibatullah Akhundzada and chief justice Abdul Hakim Haqqani (8 Jul 2025, gender persecution), Mujahid said the Taliban do not recognise any international court nor consider themselves bound by it.

relations_to.summary: The Hungarian parliament voted on 27 May 2026 (133-37) to revoke the Orban-era withdrawal from the International Criminal Court, announced during Netanyahu's April 2025 visit.

relations_to.summary: Israel challenged the Court's jurisdiction over the warrants for Netanyahu and Gallant: the Appeals Chamber (April 2025) returned the challenge to the Pre-Trial Chamber without suspending the warrants, and in October 2025 rejected Israel's bid to cancel them as repeating earlier arguments.

relations_to.summary: Use the ICC and ICJ to hold Israel to account: Palestine acceded to the Rome Statute (in force 1 Apr 2015); the Court issued warrants for Netanyahu and Gallant on 21 Nov 2024; the US cites 'taking its dispute with Israel to international courts' among its reasons for the 2026 visa ban.
